intended_object: The real Kalton–Peck space Z₂ (its underlying set): pairs (y, x) of real sequences with x ∈ ℓ₂ and y − Ω(x) ∈ ℓ₂, where Ω(x)_n = 2·x_n·log(|x_n|/‖x‖₂) is the Kalton–Peck centralizer. Inferred from the docstring, the module docs and the later instances (normed space, Banach space) put on this type.
explanation:
The type is the subtype of pairs p = (y, x) in (ℕ → ℝ) × (ℕ → ℝ) with `IsAdmissiblePair p`. That condition says x is square-summable and y − centralizer x is square-summable, with centralizer x n = 2·x_n·log(|x_n|/‖x‖₂). This is the standard twisted-sum description of the Kalton–Peck space Z₂ = ℓ₂ ⊕_Ω ℓ₂. The factor 2, i.e. x·log(x²/‖x‖²), is one of the usual normalizations in the literature. The file also proves that it matches the K₀ normalization x·log(|x|/‖x‖) up to an explicit isomorphism.

Degenerate cases come out right. Lean's convention `Real.log 0 = 0` gives Ω(x)_n = 0 when x_n = 0, and Ω(0) = 0, which is the standard convention 0·log 0 = 0. The junk value of `l2Norm` on sequences that are not square-summable never matters, because admissibility requires x ∈ ℓ₂ first.

The type is only the carrier, but the library later puts the quasi-norm-equivalent normed-space and completeness structure on it, so as a carrier it is correct. The object is specifically the *real* Kalton–Peck space, as the name and docstring say. Choosing ℝ is part of the intended object, not an unwarranted restriction, and Mathlib has no Kalton–Peck space or twisted-sum construction to defer to.
